name: PICASSO
full_name: Project In CAnada to Search for Supersymmetric Objects
summary: PICASSO used superheated fluorocarbon droplets suspended in gel to detect dark-matter nuclear recoils. It was one of the two predecessors of PICO.
detection_principle: A nuclear recoil triggers a liquid-to-gas phase transition, recorded by acoustic sensors. Temperature sets the energy threshold, and fluorine nuclei provide sensitivity to spin-dependent interactions.

results.summary: The complete dataset showed no signal consistent with dark matter and yielded final scattering limits.

science_scope: This record covers experiments that directly measure possible interactions between dark matter and ordinary matter. Published exclusion limits, background events and projected sensitivities do not constitute a dark-matter discovery.
